ordered_diagnoses: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression
salient_findings: Mass on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
key_facts: 1-year history of a gradually enlarging mass
Mass located on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
Mass located along the radial edge
Phalen’s maneuver was positive
Durkan’s test was positive
Median nerve compression indicated
Magnetic resonance imaging of the wrist was performed
Mass was well-defined and encapsulated on MRI
Mass exhibited biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign)

differentials: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents as a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the wrist with biphasic contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and present as a well-defined mass on the wrist

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a small, well-defined mass on the wrist and cause nerve compression

shortlist.label: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and present as a well-defined mass on the wrist, although less common than ganglion cyst

raw.rationale: The mass is well-defined, encapsulated, and exhibits biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) on MRI, which is characteristic of a ganglion cyst. Additionally, the location on the radial edge of the wrist and the positive Phalen’s and Durkan’s tests indicating median nerve compression are consistent with a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
rejected.why: While possible, the biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) is more characteristic of a ganglion cyst

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more solid appearance on imaging and may not exhibit the same level of encapsulation

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents with more intense pain and a distinctive appearance under the nail, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Similar to giant cell tumor of tendon sheath, but the imaging characteristics described are more typical of a ganglion cyst
